A.notes: Proactively surfaced the team's full stack without being asked: PostgreSQL for ACID financial data, Kafka event publishing (outbox pattern), gRPC for internal calls from account-service, Kotlin coroutines, Flyway already decided, correlation IDs enforced across services, and framed it as payment-service extraction from the monolith consistent with the existing service-extraction pattern. Knowledge is woven in naturally as assumptions rather than recited. Missed only the bonus signals (Sofia leading design; EKS/Kubernetes deployment not explicitly named).

B.notes: Generic payment-service checklist with no awareness of the team's stack. Assumes a third-party provider (Stripe/Braintree/Adyen) and explicitly asks 'What's your tech stack and expected transaction volume?' â€” the exact thing the system was supposed to already know. No irrelevant stored knowledge injected (because it retrieved none), so precision is technically clean, but it surfaced zero relevant context and reads as a stock answer.

analysis: System A demonstrates strong retrieval: it silently assumed Kotlin/coroutines, PostgreSQL, Kafka, gRPC with account-service, Flyway, and cross-service correlation IDs, and contextualized the task as a monolith service extraction following the established auth-service/account-service pattern â€” all without prompting the user for their stack. The knowledge feels organically woven into concrete architectural advice. System B gives competent but entirely generic guidance, defaults to an external provider, and ends by asking for the very stack/volume details the system should already have, revealing it surfaced no stored knowledge. A wins decisively on relevance and naturalness; B's only relative merit is not contaminating its answer with irrelevant context, but that is because it had no context to draw on at all.
